bihar_raw_news.content: Patna High Court directs Bihar to ensure transparency in remission records, hearing before deduction, grievance mechanisms and safeguards for prisoners under the Bihar Prison Manual. Advertisement Join WhatsApp Join Telegram The Patna High Court has issued a series of directions and recommendations to improve the remission and premature-release framework for prisoners in Bihar. The Division Bench examined how ordinary and special remission is calculated, whether the existing system permits selective treatment, and whether the Bihar Prison Manual, 2012 gives excessive discretion to prison authorities. The judgment was delivered in suo motu proceedings registered pursuant to the Supreme Court's order dated November 4, 2025, in SLP (Crl.) No. 529 of 2021. Advertisement The Court framed five questions concerning the calculation of ordinary remission, the functioning of the Remission Committee, special remission under Rules 428 and 429, the position of prisoners without education or vocational training, and the extent of executive discretion under the Bihar Prison Manual. The Bench comprising Justice Bibek Chaudhuri and Justice Chandra Shekhar Jha considered written submissions from the parties and assistance from Amicus Curiae Advocate Pratik Kumar Sinha. The Court explained that eligible convicted prisoners can earn ordinary remission based on conduct and work. Under the Manual, two days may be earned each month for good conduct and participation in institutional activities, another two days for prescribed work, and one additional day for certain work performed on Sundays and holidays. The maximum ordinary remission is seven days in a month and 84 days in a year. Advertisement The Court also directed that prisoners must receive a duplicate copy of their History Ticket showing remission earned or forfeited. "We direct that henceforth every prisoner shall be supplied with a duplicate copy of the History Ticket reflecting the remission earned or forfeited, so that the prisoner is fully informed and can seek rectification if necessary." The Bench held that the executive's discretion in remission matters is subject to safeguards. While the existing rules were not found to be "absolutely selective" or to confer excessive and unbridled power, the Court stressed transparency, reasoned decisions and natural justice. In particular, before remission already granted is deducted or seized, the prisoner must be given an opportunity of hearing and a reasoned order must follow. The Court noted that special remission under Rule 428 is available to all convicted prisoners without an educational qualification. However, Rule 429 provides an additional incentive to long-term prisoners who assist in improving educational standards or imparting vocational training. Advertisement To address possible inequality, the Court directed the State to examine whether an alternative route could be created for illiterate prisoners to earn comparable additional remission through other reformative or institutional contributions. The Court recommended fixed timelines for premature-release proceedings, including initiating the process at least six months before the eligibility date. It also recommended mechanisms for correcting remission calculations, appeals against seizure, and greater transparency regarding life convicts' remission and premature-release cases. bihar_raw_news.title: Objections mount over draft KU rules restricting campus politics | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 21, 2026 Objections mount over draft KU rules restricting campus politics Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Objections have mounted against a draft Kerala University Students’ Code of Conduct Regulations that propose restrictions on political activities on campus and at affiliated colleges, even as university officials say nothing has been finalised or implemented. The university syndicate recently considered the draft regulations, which include restrictions on student organisations conducting protests, dharnas, recruiting new members, putting up posters and graffiti on walls, soliciting funds, organising events featuring political personalities and conducting online campaigning, according to members of the Left-aligned Kerala University Employees’ Union. Union members said the draft gives heads of departments on the university campus and principals of affiliated colleges powers to take action, including suspension, against students found violating the proposed rules. They said students involved in violent activities could face a one-year suspension, while proposed penalties include Rs 5,000 for students, Rs 10,000 for political organisations and Rs one lakh for repeated violations. Unpaid fines would be treated as arrears and could lead to procedures including revenue recovery and potential property attachment, withholding of examination results and criminal proceedings under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act. The Kerala University Employees’ Union has opposed the proposed regulations, saying they are an attempt to restrict political activities on campuses and are undemocratic. The union said it will launch protests if the regulations are implemented, alleging that such restrictions would curtail students’ participation in organisational activities. Resmi R, Registrar of Kerala University, told PTI on Sunday that only a draft has been prepared and it is yet to be finalised. “The syndicate meeting discussed the Code of Conduct Regulations and only a draft based on a similar code at MG University, Kottayam, and a High Court order has been prepared. The final code will be brought out only after discussions with stakeholders, including students,” she said. She said no order has been issued to implement the proposed regulations. Meanwhile, Leader of the Opposition in the Keralam Assembly, Pinarayi Vijayan, condemned the proposed restrictions on student organisations on campuses, saying attempts to drive politics and political awareness out of campuses stemmed from a fear of a generation that asks questions. In a Facebook post on Saturday night, Vijayan said the decision appeared to be part of an agenda of those disturbed by student movements that had emerged across the country. “If those behind this anti-democratic decision do not withdraw from it, Keralam is certain to witness strong protests,” he said. Vijayan said the Constitution gives every citizen who turns 18 the right to vote and participate in choosing governments, and argued that denying young people the right to think politically, organise and respond while studying in educational institutions was unconstitutional and amounted to complete depoliticisation. national_raw_news.content: Marking a new chapter in Indian cinema, President Droupadi Murmu will present the historic 72nd National Film Awards this evening at Ekta Nagar. Instituted in 1954, these awards represent India’s highest cinematic honours, recognising artistic and technical excellence across various categories, namely Feature, Non-Feature, and Writing on Cinema. As part of a major policy initiative by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, the awards are being held outside the national capital. The ceremony at Ekta Nagar brings together cinematic talent from across the country, embodying the spirit of ‘Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat’. The president will also honour the veteran actor Anant Nag with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024. The stage is set, and the lights are ready in the iconic Ekta Nagar as Kevadia prepares to host the historic 72nd National Film Awards for the very first time. Renowned actors, acclaimed filmmakers, and technicians from across the country have started arriving at the venue for this grand celebration of Indian cinema. The ceremony honours outstanding cinematic achievements for the year 2024. Among the major feature film announcements, Article 370 was selected for Best Feature Film, with Yami Gautam winning Best Actress for her role in the film. The Best Actor honour is shared by Mammootty for Bramayugam and Kartik Aaryan for Chandu Champion. Rajkumar Periasamy earned Best Direction for Amaran, while Kalki 2898 AD was named Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Randeep Hooda won Best Debut Director for Swatantrya Veer Savarkar. In the non-feature category, the Marathi film Bhangaar was named Best Non-Feature Film, while Director Aanand L Rai was selected for Best Direction for Statue of Unity – Ekta ka Prateek. Ravi Raj Murmu took the Best Debut Director (Non-Feature) honour for the Santhali film, Angen.

national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 144 EAM S Jaishankar holds talks with France, Ecuador, Slovakia, Switzerland counterparts in New York
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar held talks with his counterparts from France, Ecuador, Slovakia and Switzerland on the sidelines of UN General Assembly in New York last night and discussed regional and global issues. Mr Jaishankar arrived in New York City on Sunday, leading the Indian delegation for the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. Mr Jaishankar will address world leaders at the General Debate from the UNGA podium on September 26. His engagements commenced with a meeting with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot. In a social media post Mr Jaishankar said the regular meetings and telecons enable both countries to maintain the momentum of Special Global Strategic Partnership. He said that during the meeting, regional and global issues, specifically the Ukraine and Gulf crises, were discussed. Both the leaders also exchanged views on multilateral issues, including the reform of UN Security Council. External Affairs Minister also held a meeting with Ecuador Foreign Minister Roberto Kury, to strengthen economic ties, including energy and pharmaceuticals, mobility, training of personnel, development partnership and cooperation in multilateral fora, including the United Nations. Following his meeting with Slovakia Foreign Minister Juraj Blanar, the External Affairs Minister said that besides discussing the bilateral agenda, they also touched upon ways to deepen our multilateral cooperation. Mr. Jaishankar also held a meeting with Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Hungary Anita Orban. Both the leaders have agreed to work together to deepen ties to advance the bilateral strategic partnership. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held separate meetings with Switzerland Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis and Nauru President David Adeang, discussing bilateral ties, economic cooperation, and multilateral issues. Sharing details of his meeting on a social media post , Mr Jaishankar said the two sides reviewed the progress in their economic relationship following the entry into force of the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement. Earlier, Dr Jaishankar attended the first Visegrád Group (V4) and India Foreign Ministers’ Meeting, involving Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic.

national_raw_news.title: Sikkim’s natural farming journey reflects PM Modi’s vision of Viksit Bharat 1 hour ago 26
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Apart from mystic lakes and snow-capped mountains, Sikkim is famous for its vast agricultural offerings not only in India but also to the world. Sikkim has been declared the 1st Organic State in 2016 and is famous for crops like large cardamom, ginger buckwheat etc. Sikkim produces around 90% of large cardamom, which is Highest Large Cardamom in India, and exported to countries like Australia and the UAE. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Beema Yojana has played a pivotal role in the natural farming scenario in Sikkim. Apart from Large Cardamom, Buckwheat is one of the crops that’s extensively harvested in Sikkim which is around 1600kg per hector. Being the 3rd largest crop and 2nd most common cereal crop in Sikkim Buckwheat has a GI Certification. With time and with firm collaboration with Govt of India, ICAR Sikkim and Department of Agriculture, Govt of Sikkim the scene of Natural Farming as well as Organic Farming is growing stronger in Sikkim.

national_raw_news.title: Jharkhand celebrates Karam festival with cultural programmes and traditional rituals 3 hours ago 55
national_raw_news.content: Karam festival, a vibrant celebration of Jharkhand’s rich tribal culture, nature and the bond between brothers and sisters, is being observed across the state today with traditional fervour and enthusiasm. Special cultural and state-level programmes are being organised across Jharkhand to mark the auspicious occasion. Karam festival, one of the most significant celebrations of Jharkhand’s folk culture and nature worship, is being celebrated across the state today with great enthusiasm. Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar attended the program on the eve of Karam festival organised in Bero, Ranchi, as the chief guest and extended greetings to the people of the state. He also delivered a message on nature conservation. Yesterday, a seminar-cum-cultural programme was organised at Audrey House in Ranchi, where the entire premises came alive with Jharkhand’s cultural spirit to the beats of drums, nagadas and mandar, accompanied by traditional Karam songs. A programme was also organised yesterday evening at the Deekshant Mandap in Morabadi, where a tribal fashion show was the main attraction. Karam festival is considered a symbol of crop protection, respect for nature, and the enduring bond between brothers and sisters. On this occasion, sisters observe a Nirjala fast, praying for the well-being and long life of their brothers. This evening, a sacred branch of the Karam tree will be installed at the akhara, followed by community dances and traditional songs throughout the night. In Ranchi, the state capital, as well as in various parts of the state, arrangements have been made for cleanliness, lighting, drinking water and other essential civic facilities at Karam worship sites and akharas. Administrative officials have also reviewed preparations for the Karam festival and have participated in various events.
